wo simultaneous identical requests currently both miss the store and both call the provider. The implementation therefore does not yet support its “provider called once” / duplicate-accounting claim.
Treat reuse of an existing key with a different fingerprint as an idempotency conflict, not as a new request that overwrites the old record. The current behavior makes one key oscillate between unrelated payloads and hides caller misuse.
Namespace keys by trusted principal/tenant rather than putting tenant only in the fingerprint. The current global dict[key] lets different tenants overwrite each other's idempotency records. Given tenant-less credentials exist, a trusted credential_id is likely part of the correct namespace.

I would also replace repr()-based fingerprints with an explicitly canonical serialized payload before this becomes a durable-storage contract.

Your four scope decisions otherwise mostly hold: non-streaming idempotency is a sensible exclusion; model resolution should precede lookup; tenant must absolutely participate in isolation; and exposing idempotency_status is useful and appropriate. The main issue is that the store currently records completed past calls, but does not yet coordinate calls happening now or provide a stable ownership namespace—and those are core idempotency properties rather than optional refinements.
